chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

That ʿAlī عليه السلام used to administer taʿzīr in satirical abuse, and he would not inflict the hadd except in explicit false accusation: that one says, ‘O fornicator,’ ‘O son of a fornicating woman,’ or ‘You do not belong to your father.’

key_terms.لَسْتَ لِأَبِيكَ: a denial of a person's attribution to his father
key_terms.يُعَزِّرُ: he administers discretionary punishment short of the fixed hadd

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment applied for slander or insult in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام distinguished between general abusive satire and explicit defamatory accusation. He applied discretionary punishment in invective, but the fixed hadd penalty only in clear statements of false accusation against chastity or lineage.
